pages.body:
Your AI receptionist answers on a real phone number, around the clock, on the first ring. It greets callers in a voice that fits your brand, answers questions from your own information (hours, services, prices, policies), takes messages, and books consultations or routes calls the way you would.

## Hear it for yourself

Call our 24/7 Voice Agent/receptionist at **[(765) 307-5537](tel:+17653075537)**. She answers for AH Media, trained on our knowledge base and can answer questions and book appointments. Yours would be trained on your own business.

## What a missed call costs

Every call that goes to voicemail is a customer who might call the next business on the list. The math is simple:

**missed calls a week × average job value × how often a call books = revenue walking away**

Say you miss 5 calls a week, an average booking is worth $300, and 3 in 10 callers book. That's $450 a week, more than $23,000 a year, walking out the door. We run this with your real numbers on the first call.

## You own everything

Your phone number, phone account and AI voice account are all in your business's name, on your own card, not ours. We set them up, connect them, and walk you through the carrier registration that keeps your calls from being flagged as spam. We manage and tune your receptionist with access you grant, and if you ever leave, all of it goes with you.

## How it works

1. **Discovery:** a call about your business, what callers usually ask, and roughly how many calls you get on a busy day.
2. **Conversation design:** we script how she greets, answers, books and hands off, and pick a voice that fits your brand.
3. **Training:** she learns your services, prices, hours and policies from your own information.
4. **Go live:** we connect your number and test it with you before real callers reach her.
5. **Tuning:** we review real calls and keep tightening her answers.

## Connects to the rest of your business

Pair her with [Automations](/services/automations) to send call summaries to your inbox, log callers in your CRM, or follow up by email after a booking.

## Who it's for

Med spas, clinics, salons and service businesses where a missed call is a missed booking, especially when the front desk is busy with the people already in the room.

## Getting started

Sold separately from the website packages. Setup and ongoing management are quoted once we know your call volume, and call usage is billed directly to the accounts in your name with no markup from us. [Get in touch](/contact) to talk it through.

pages.title: Second Brain
pages.hero_subheading: Your own agentic OS: a folder of plain files, LLM agents that read and write them, and scripts that keep it honest.
pages.section_heading: Files + LLMs + scripts = your Second Brain
pages.body:
A second brain is where your business remembers things: plans, decisions, clients, notes, and what happened last Tuesday. Ours are built from three simple parts, so they're cheap to run, easy to change, and never locked in to one vendor.

![How a second brain fits together: Human:IO, your files, LLM agents, and scripts and hooks](/images/second-brain-diagram.svg)

## The Human:IO layer

The part you touch. Talk to it with a voice note from your phone, chat with it in your terminal or browser, or read and edit it in [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md). Each morning it can hand you a short brief of open to-dos and unfinished plans. You never have to learn where things are filed; the agents do the filing.

## Your files

Everything lives in a folder of plain Markdown files with a little structured data at the top: one folder per project, with its plans, session logs and lessons learned, plus people, patterns and references. Plain files mean you own them, they sync anywhere, and any tool, human or AI, can read them.

## LLM agents

Agents like Claude Code work inside the folder. **Context files** tell them how your business works, **skills** teach them repeatable jobs (log the session, start a project, record a takeaway), and **memory** carries what they learned from one session to the next.

## Scripts and hooks

Anything that must come out the same every time is a script, not a prompt. Hooks run at the start and end of each session to brief you and log the work; small edit scripts check off to-dos and update plan status without ever mangling a file; n8n workflows bring in voice notes and other outside input.

## What you get

A working second brain set up around how you already work, the context files and skills to run it, and a walkthrough so you can extend it yourself.

case_studies.title: Dream World Cirque: a brand pass
case_studies.summary: A Los Angeles cirque company whose site hid its own spectacle. We rebuilt it layer by layer until it looked like a circus poster, not a template.
case_studies.narrative:
## The starting point

Dream World Cirque is a boutique aerial and cirque company in Los Angeles: contortionists, aerialists, fire and LED acts, and performers with backgrounds in Cirque du Soleil and professional ballet. Their old site, built years ago in Adobe Muse, told almost none of that. A carousel competed with the logo, the calls to action were buried, and the contact form had been quietly sending enquiries to an old mailbox for years.

We started with an audit of the old site, then rebuilt it. Building fast with AI tools carries a specific risk: everything drifts towards the same defaults. The same fonts, the same gradients, the same centred hero with three icon cards underneath. The brand pass is how we stopped that from happening.

## Layer by layer

- **Type.** When we asked for "distinctive" fonts, the suggestions were the same handful of elegant serifs that every AI-assisted redesign reaches for. We went the other way: a decorative display face with the character of a vintage circus poster for the hero, and a quiet sans for everything else, so the performers stay the focus.
- **Fonts that actually load.** The audit turned up a real bug: the body and heading fonts were named in the CSS but never delivered, so most visitors saw a system fallback. It only looked right on machines that happened to have the fonts installed. We self-hosted the real files.
- **Colour and hero.** The palette comes straight from the stage lighting in their own photos: purple, hot pink and amber. The hero is a muted, looping performance video under a brand-coloured overlay, tuned so the footage reads and the type stays legible.
- **Details.** The real hand-drawn crest in the header, a subject-matched icon for every service instead of one generic arrow, and photo-led sections in place of a template grid.

## The result

A site that looks like Dream World Cirque and no one else, built on a CMS the team can update directly, with an AI-assisted pipeline behind it that classifies and drafts replies to incoming enquiries. The gallery below shows the method: an illustrative "AI default" version of the site next to the real one, the type decision, and each layer applied in turn.

case_studies.title: Monk Magazine: hacked-site recovery
case_studies.summary: Monk Magazine’s customers saw a red "deceptive site" warning. Behind it: six weeks of hidden admin access. We traced it, cleaned it and locked it down.
case_studies.narrative:
## How it surfaced

Monk Magazine is an independent magazine that sells its print and digital issues through its own online store. A customer reported a red "Deceptive Website Warning" when visiting the site. We started investigating the same day. The domain itself hadn't been hijacked; the warning came from a fake "security check" popup injected into the site's theme and into six published posts.

## What we found

An attacker had logged in with a stolen admin password and spent about six weeks building ways back in:

- **Six malicious plugins**, one of them hiding the attacker's accounts from the admin screen
- **A login-stealing plugin** posing as an analytics add-on, quietly sending every admin login to an outside server
- **Two hidden administrator accounts** and **two fake themes** that let the attacker run commands
- **49 copies** of the injected popup and **13 scheduled tasks** that reinstalled parts of the infection after removal
- A **1.1 GB full-site backup** sitting in a public folder where anyone could download it

## Cleaning it up, then checking again

The first sweep removed the plugins, accounts, popup and scheduled tasks, and rotated the site's security keys. A second sweep the next day found the better-disguised wave: the fake themes and the login stealer. Attackers rarely leave just one way back in, so we kept looking. A deeper review of the server logs later found **two more backdoor files** in a folder the first sweeps hadn't covered. They were removed the same day, the attacker was blocked, and every password and key was changed.

## Locked down

Plugin and theme uploads from the dashboard were switched off, code was blocked from running in upload folders, eight unused plugins were removed, paid downloads were moved out of the public web folder, and a daily integrity check now flags any unexpected change the next morning. A clean copy of the site was also rebuilt on new, isolated hosting. The final re-scan came back clean. Since then the site's security add-on has blocked more than 144,000 login attempts, about 300 a day, every one refused.

## What the client needed to do

Our report also covered the decisions only the owners could make: rotating payment provider keys together on a short call, whether to notify customers, and adding a second owner to the payment accounts so the business no longer depends on one phone.

It's done in 3 days, or 24 hours if it's urgent. WordPress is the most common case, but we work on any site we can get server access to.

You talk to it by voice, chat or Obsidian. See Second Brain.
